search_log: Searched “Patricia Cornwell Predator novel excerpt chapter point of view third person” and opened the ABC News excerpt plus explicit POV discussions from ABC News and The Washington Post.

Searched official author and publisher domains for Predator excerpts; Patricia Cornwell, Penguin Random House, and Hachette pages verified the work but their synopsis language was not used as person evidence.
Searched Google Books and exact excerpt phrases for additional opening or interior prose; results did not provide a separately usable sustained preview.

Searched “Predator Patricia Cornwell epistolary diary frame narrative,” “alternating point of view,” and “multiple narrators”; found descriptions of multiple character perspectives but no credible evidence of first- or second-person base sections.
person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages represent characters in third person, while all visible first- and second-person forms occur in dialogue, aphorisms, or generic thought content. A sustained web excerpt independently shows third-person present narration, and two credible articles explicitly describe Predator’s whole-book mode as omniscient third person. The novel shifts among character perspectives, but those perspectives remain within third-person narration, so this is not person-level alternation. No credible contrary or frame/epistolary evidence was found.
